title: Kimi K3 on iac-bench 2026-10
summary: How Kimi K3 did on iac-bench 2026-10: an overall composite of 82.4, scores per fixture, strengths, weaknesses and the patterns in its OpenTofu modules.
body_markdown:
Developer Moonshot AI


API identifier` moonshotai/kimi-k3`


Access OpenRouter


Weights Open


List price (USD / M tokens, in / out) 0.24 / 11.94 (OpenRouter, 2026-10-23)


Evaluated 2026-10-22 (generation) · 2026-10-23 (judge)


Attempts 9 (3 fixtures × 3 samples)


**Overall composite** **82.4** (95% CI 57.3–84.7)


Rank 5 of 10 (95% rank interval 5–9)


Mechanical only / judge only 80.6 (rank 5) / 86.0 (rank 6)


Failed gates · insecure attempts 1/9 · 4/9


Estimated cost, all 9 attempts $3.96


## Summary


Kimi K3 is the highest-scoring open-weight model in the release, placing in the second group just behind the leaders. Its App Service median of 87 is close to the top of the field. Its modules are heavily validated, put identity first, and split into conventional files. Its interfaces are large.


All four of its security findings come from the same habit: a secure default that a consumer can override through an input. On Cloud SQL,` ssl_mode` defaults to` ENCRYPTED_ONLY` , but the validation also accepts` ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED_AND_ENCRYPTED` . This happens in all three attempts, and the variable's description itself says the setting should not be weakened.

Definitions are in[Scoring criteria](https://www.massdriver.cloud/blogs/iac-bench-2026-10-scoring-criteria) .


## Strengths


- **S3 hardening,** in 3/3 attempts:


- bucket-owner-enforced ownership;
- cleanup of incomplete multipart uploads;
- a TLS-deny bucket policy;
- the regional domain output.


- **Identity-first database access.** IAM database login, workload identities, customer-managed key support and Query Insights in 3/3 attempts. Password users are deliberately unsupported, and it strips the service-account suffix that Cloud SQL rejects.
- **Validation in depth.** 14–20 validation blocks per Cloud SQL module, including cross-field checks such as "point-in-time recovery requires backups."
- **Hardcoded posture on App Service.** HTTPS-only, TLS 1.2 and FTPS-off are not inputs. The planned attempts earned E1–E4.


## Weaknesses


- **Cloud SQL` H2` (security finding, 3/3).** The` ssl_mode` validation admits unencrypted connections (excerpt below). The judge scored *Anti-patterns* 0 in all three attempts. Here the two components agree.
- **S3` H1` (security finding, 1/3).** One attempt adds` allow_public_read` , which turns off all four public-access-block settings and grants public` s3:GetObject` .
- **Failed gate on App Service (1/3).** The staging slot sets` health_check_path` without` health_check_eviction_time_in_min` , which the provider requires together. The production app sets both.
- **Large interfaces.** Over budget on S3 in 3/3 attempts and on App Service in both attempts that planned (27 and 34 inputs).
- **Lifecycle and pinning gaps:**


- no database` deletion_policy` (` H11` , 3/3);
- S3 logging without a delivery grant (` H13` , 3/3);
- ` B1` lost in 5 of the 8 attempts that planned.


- **Validation that rejects valid values.** It caps transaction-log retention at 7 days, but Enterprise Plus allows 35.


## Characteristic patterns


- **Secure default, open override:** the source of every security finding. The same posture is hardcoded on App Service, so the habit is not universal.
- **Long transcripts.** 22–49k median output tokens per attempt, the most in the field on Cloud SQL. Every attempt ships a README and` minimal.tfvars` .
- **Provider blocks present on GCP and Azure, absent on AWS** (` H15` , 3/3).


## Representative excerpt


` G002/kimi-k3-e1/variables.tf` lines 200–209


```text
variable "ssl_mode" {
description = "TLS enforcement for connections. The organizational standard is ENCRYPTED_ONLY; TRUSTED_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED additionally demands mutual TLS. Do not weaken this without a security review."
type        = string
default     = "ENCRYPTED_ONLY"


validation {
condition     = contains(["ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED_AND_ENCRYPTED", "ENCRYPTED_ONLY", "TRUSTED_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED"], var.ssl_mode)
error_message = "ssl_mode must be one of ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED_AND_ENCRYPTED, ENCRYPTED_ONLY or TRUSTED_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED."
}
}


```


The description states the standard and warns against weakening it, yet the validation accepts the unencrypted mode. That one list entry cost` H2` in all three Cloud SQL attempts.
